citation.source: Reuses tortilla_mixture.json's own just-computed values directly, not a fresh derivation — see that file's own citation for the full potato:egg 3:1 Choi-Okos derivation.
citation.note: A deliberate simplification: onion's real proportion in this dish is much smaller than potato/egg (roughly one onion per ~1kg potato), and onion.json's own composition (89% water) is similarly water-dominated to potato/egg's, so this repo treats its effect on the composite's bulk thermophysical properties as negligible rather than computing a third, separately-weighted composite for a likely-imperceptible difference — named explicitly as a simplification, not silently assumed identical.

metadata.notes: A DELIBERATELY SEPARATE entity from tortilla_mixture.json, not the same entity reused — the honest reason ROADMAP.md named this as a real, unbuilt gap rather than something a capability flag could paper over: structure.components ['potato','onion','egg'] genuinely differs from plain tortilla_mixture's ['potato','egg'], and this repo's own structure.composite/components field exists specifically to keep that kind of compositional fact truthful, not collapse two different dishes into one entity id for convenience. Everything else (possibleStates/possibleTags/invalidTransitions/capabilities/criticalControlPointsByAction) mirrors tortilla_mixture.json exactly — see that entity's own notes for the reasoning behind each, unchanged here: the egg-risk CCP, the flipped-as-tag-not-state choice, the known one-side-vs-both-sides-fried gap, and the burned/overcooked TICKET-5 entries all apply identically, since egg's contribution to this composite is physically the same regardless of what else is mixed in with the potato.
metadata.sensoryNote: taste gains 'sweet' (kept alongside 'neutral', not replacing it) relative to plain tortilla_mixture.json — a direct, real consequence of the onion having been caramelized/confit-fried into the base before combining, not an arbitrary difference between the two entities.
metadata.restNote: isRestable + REST, mirroring tortilla_mixture.json's identical addition 2026-08-16 — see that file's own restNote/rawStateHonestyNote for the full reasoning (unchanged here: egg's real contact-heat pre-cooking and flavor-absorption effects apply identically regardless of whether onion is also present in the base).
metadata.knownGap: Same as tortilla_mixture.json's identical field: FRY applied twice (before/after FLIP) both just set the fixed state 'fried', with no way to distinguish one side fried from both sides fully cooked.
metadata.failureStateNote: 'burned'/'overcooked' mirror tortilla_mixture.json's identical TICKET-5 entries — see that file's own note for the full reasoning (unconditionally terminal 'burned', 'overcooked' leaves 'burned' reachable, isTerminalState correctly computes false for 'overcooked').
